name: Fairmont Chateau Laurier
insider_take: This iconic castle-like hotel has been Ottawa's crown jewel since 1912, hosting royalty, prime ministers, and dignitaries while anchoring the capital's most prestigious corner.
whats_special: The Fairmont Chateau Laurier is literally steps from Parliament Hill and directly connected to Ottawa's Central Station via underground tunnels. This Gothic Revival masterpiece features limestone turrets and copper roofs that have defined Ottawa's skyline for over a century. The hotel's Confederation Lounge offers unparalleled views of the Ottawa River and Gatineau Hills, while its grand ballrooms have witnessed countless historic political moments and state functions.
pro_tip: Book a Heritage Room facing the Parliament Buildings for front-row seats to Canada Day celebrations and the Changing of the Guard ceremony, plus use the underground walkway to explore downtown Ottawa year-round without braving harsh Canadian winters.
dont_miss: The hotel's Camera Museum showcases vintage photography equipment, while the original 1912 Peacock Alley corridor displays historical artifacts. Visit Wilfrid's Restaurant, named after Canada's first francophone Prime Minister, and take advantage of the prime location to walk to the Rideau Canal (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), ByWard Market, and the National Gallery of Canada—all within a 5-minute stroll.
pros: Historic castle-like architecture with iconic Ottawa landmark status
Prime downtown location steps from Parliament Hill and ByWard Market
Elegant luxury accommodations with classic European charm
Exceptional service standards and fine dining options
cons: Heritage building may have older room configurations
Premium pricing reflects luxury positioning and prime location
